- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) in recent days, reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike (≥ 10% above recent mean) followed by a drop, cap the peak and adjust downward by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.15) and forecast is consistently above true price, apply a 3–5% downward correction to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true price deviates > 3% from forecast in first 5–7 days, adjust future days downward by 1–2% per day to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive signals (0.06–0.11) but forecast is overoptimistic, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, reduce forecast by 5–8% in the following 3–5 days to reflect sentiment reversal.
